summary: Widely loved for its smoky pineapple scent and the compliments it earns, and a regular pick for dates, work and special occasions. Performance is the divide: many report it fading to a skin scent within a few hours, especially from recent batches, while others get a full day. Many also question the high price.

A fresh, green, clean fougère that fans call a favorite and a classic, popular in warm weather and easy to wear. The main complaint is that it fades fast or hardly projects, and several say recent batches are weaker than older ones. Some feel it is not worth the price, and a few find it dated.

A powdery, creamy iris scent that reviewers find elegant and dressy, best for dates, evenings and special occasions, and it brings compliments. The main downside is staying power and projection, with several saying recent bottles are weaker than older ones. Those who dislike iris find it powdery, feminine or old-fashioned.

A crisp, clean, tea-like freshness that reviewers love for warm days and the office, with frequent compliments. The main complaint is poor staying power, with many getting only a few hours and a soft skin scent, which they find hard to justify at the price. A few find it inky or bland.

A warm, sweet vanilla and cinnamon gourmand often compared to Parfums de Marly Althair, mostly worn in cold weather. Fans praise the compliments, longevity and price. Some get weak projection or short wear, and others find it too sweet, synthetic or harsh in the opening, which can improve with rest.

A sweet, airy gourmand that most owners love for the many compliments and low price. The main letdown is staying power, with many getting only a few hours, though some report it lasting a day or more. A fair number find it synthetic, plasticky or headache-inducing.

Most reviewers get a bright grapefruit citrus that dries down musky and woody, with long wear, compliments and strong value for a budget blue. The opening can smell harsh or synthetic until the bottle has rested for a couple of months. Some get short wear or weak projection, and a few dislike the musky base.

A fresh, metallic citrus in the Silver Mountain Water mould that most reviewers find strong and long-lasting, with plenty of compliments for the price. The opening is often sharp or synthetic and tends to soften with rest. A few get weak wear, and some dislike the metallic edge.

A spicy, minty barbershop fougère that fans call a standout Creed, with sweet warm woods in the drydown. It divides people, and some find it old-fashioned or hard to wear. Longevity is mixed, with some getting a full day and others a few hours, and it leans toward cooler weather.

A very sweet, boozy cinnamon and apple-pie style gourmand that most reviewers love for compliments, strong projection and a low price. It suits cold weather and nights out. The main complaint is that it is too sweet, cloying or feminine for some, and a few find it cheap-smelling or gone quickly.

A clean, musky skin scent that most reviewers love, with frequent compliments and good staying power on many. Projection varies a lot, with some finding it soft and close and others finding it loud. A fair number find it metallic, chemical or simply cannot smell it on their skin.

A clean, soapy, lightly sweet scent often compared to YSL Y, liked as an easy office or daily pick. Performance is the split: some get many hours and days on clothes, while many get only a few hours and modest projection. Scent is generally well liked at the price.

A salty, fruity melon aquatic that many reviewers say resembles Creed Millésime Impérial while lasting longer. It is praised for longevity, compliments and price, and suits hot weather. The opening can smell odd or metallic and needs time for some, and a few find it too feminine or never warm to it.

A Bleu de Chanel style blue that most reviewers find long-lasting, versatile and good value, with regular compliments. The opening is often harsh or synthetic until the bottle has rested. Some get weak projection or little staying power, and a few blame their batch.

A sweet apple, vanilla and spice scent with strong projection that earns many compliments and works across seasons. The main objection is a medicinal menthol opening that some compare to Vicks, which others find fades into a lovely drydown. A few get weak staying power or say recent batches are weaker.

A tart rhubarb, lychee and rose scent that has devoted fans and a reputation for compliments. Reviewers are split, though, and a lot find it too sour, sweet, synthetic or generic for the price. Several note it smells very different on different skin.

A warm, sweet vanilla and chestnut scent that reviewers love for cold weather and regular compliments, with good projection. Some find it too sweet. A number say it fades within hours, and several say recent batches are weaker than older bottles.

A sweet mandarin that dries down to caramel, liked mostly for compliments and decent staying power, especially in cooler weather. Some find it synthetic, headache-inducing or too sweet, and a few get little projection. It often improves after a few weeks of rest.

A restrained, dry woody take on oud with cedar, sandalwood and spice, which many reviewers call their favorite Creed. It suits cooler weather and special occasions. The main complaints are modest staying power and a steep price, and a few find it sickly, cloying or irritating on their skin.

A fresh, salty, fruity citrus with a clean, summery feel that many call their favorite Creed. By far the main complaint is poor performance, with many getting only a couple of hours and little projection, though some get a full day. A few find it musty or melony.
